You are a careful, neutral coder of the STRUCTURE OF A CORPORATE TRANSACTION AT
CLOSING. You are given ONE evidence slice assembled from public primary sources
(SEC filings, company releases, reputable press). This slice describes ONLY how the
deal was structured -- what crossed the ownership boundary and what did not -- at
the moment of closing. You are DELIBERATELY NOT shown what happened to the combined
company afterward, and you must NOT speculate about later outcomes, success, or
failure. Code STRICTLY the deal as structured. If the slice does not let you
determine a field, you MUST return "uncertain" -- never guess, never infer from
outside knowledge of the companies.

Emit a single structured record with these fields.

A. BUNDLE SIGNATURE -- for each of six organizational tiers, classify what happened
to that tier when the transaction crossed the ownership boundary. Exactly one label
per tier.
  T1 Owner Intent (controlling principal / imprint).
     Labels: replace, imprint-share, continue, terminate, reconstruct, replicate, mutual-replace, uncertain.
       replace = old controlling intent exited, a new one installed;
       imprint-share = both principals' intent co-present;
       continue = same controlling intent persists;
       terminate = the controlling intent ended with no successor;
       reconstruct = intent re-formed into a new (often non-commercial) purpose;
       replicate = intent copied into a standardized template (e.g. franchising);
       mutual-replace = two intents fused into a jointly-new one (merger of equals).
  T2 Business Model, T3 Business Entity (legal vehicle), T4 Product (customer-
  acceptance layer), T5 Process (operations), T6 Organization (people/culture).
     Labels for T2-T6: 1-1, N-1, 1-N, subset, partial, read-only, swap, terminate, null, uncertain.
       1-1 = transferred whole, one-to-one; N-1 = many collapsed into one;
       1-N = one split into many; subset = only part transferred;
       partial = transferred but incompletely / with friction;
       read-only = licensed / accessed without ownership transfer;
       swap = exchanged for a different one (e.g. new legal domicile);
       terminate = ended; null = not applicable / nothing at this tier.

B. TIER-TRANSFER GAPS -- code strictly from the STRUCTURE OF THE DEAL AT CLOSING.
A gap is a STRUCTURAL MISMATCH IN WHAT THE DEAL TRANSFERRED, not a later failure.
  gap_45: Did the customer-facing product/asset (T4, what customers buy) cross the
    ownership boundary WITHOUT the operational processes that produce or deliver it
    (T5) transferring or being aligned coherently alongside it? A documented
    product-vs-process structural mismatch AT CLOSING. 1 = yes such a gap; 0 = no
    (product and its processes moved together, or neither moved); uncertain.
  gap_56: Did the operational processes (T5) transfer or get re-engineered WITHOUT
    the organization / people / management / culture that run them (T6) transferring
    or aligning coherently alongside, AT CLOSING? 1 = yes; 0 = no; uncertain.
  gap_mitigated: If (and only if) you coded a structural gap above, was that gap
    documented as contractually absorbed at closing via a transitional-services or
    operating agreement allocating the shared substrate? yes / no / NA (NA if no gap).

E. collapse_state: Any Tier-1 fusion documented in the deal structure? none /
   T1=T4 (founder identity IS the product) / T1=T3 (the legal subject IS a specific
   natural person) / T1=T3=T4 / T1=T2 / T1=T6 / uncertain.

rationale: 2-4 sentences citing the slice lines that drove your gap_45 and gap_56
codes specifically. Cite ONLY closing-structure evidence; do NOT reason about later
outcomes.

Emit ONLY the structured record. Code conservatively: inability to determine a
structural field is "uncertain"; a gap you cannot document at closing is 0.

# Structural sub-dossier — Inland Western Retail Real Estate Trust, Inc., corporate and portfolio structure around the drawn filing date (October 2010)

> EVIDENTIARY STANDARD: every factual line ends with a `[SRC: <SEC accession / URL>]`
> tag pointing to a public primary source. A fact that cannot be so sourced is written
> `[UNVERIFIED]` and is never guessed. This sub-dossier describes ONLY the entity's
> corporate/organizational structure and the content of the closing-era filings
> reviewed for this case. It contains no post-2010 outcome information.

## What the drawn filing establishes
- The drawn filing is a Form 8-K dated October 15, 2010 (accession 0001104659-10-052516)
  reporting: (Item 5.02) board-approved increases to the base salaries of four named
  officers effective January 1, 2011, and a change in the bonus arrangement to pay
  bonuses in company stock rather than cash; (Item 5.03) a bylaws amendment permitting
  designation of several vice-president levels and deleting a stockholder-records-access
  provision; (Item 5.07) results of the October 12, 2010 annual stockholders' meeting
  (director election, charter amendment and restatement, independent-director stock
  option plan, all approved); and (Item 7.01) furnishing a related press release.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-10-052516, Form 8-K Items 5.02/5.03/5.07/7.01/9.01]
- This filing reports governance, compensation, and annual-meeting matters; it does not
  report or reference a merger, acquisition, or other business-combination closing.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-10-052516, Form 8-K]
- The furnished Exhibit 99.1 press release states that, as of June 30, 2010, the entity
  is a "self-managed real estate investment trust" with a portfolio exceeding 46 million
  square feet across 294 consolidated operating properties, 11 unconsolidated operating
  properties, and 8 properties under development. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-10-052516, Form 8-K Ex-99.1]
- The same press release reports year-to-date items including refinancing of 83% of 2010
  debt maturities, a new definitive joint-venture agreement (initial $123 million) with
  RioCan REIT under which it had closed on three of eight initial properties, and the
  sale of five assets for $80 million (extinguishing $61 million of debt).
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-10-052516, Form 8-K Ex-99.1]

## Contemporaneous filings confirm no discrete acquisition closing near this date
- An 8-K dated October 8, 2010 furnished a letter to stockholders concerning the third-
  quarter 2010 distribution. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-10-051800, Form 8-K]
- An 8-K dated October 12, 2010 furnished presentation materials shown at the annual
  meeting. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-10-052021, Form 8-K]
- An 8-K dated October 22, 2010 furnished a stockholder mailing in which the board
  recommended stockholders REJECT an unsolicited tender offer for less than 5% of the
  company's common shares. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-10-053237, Form 8-K]
- A review of the entity's 2010 EDGAR filing index (forms 8-K, 10-K, S-4, DEFM14A) found
  no S-4 or DEFM14A (merger-registration or merger-proxy) filing in 2010. [SRC: SEC EDGAR filing index, CIK 1222840, forms 8-K/10-K/S-4/DEFM14A, calendar 2010]

## Entity structure and history (from the FY2009 Form 10-K, the closing-era annual report)
- The entity describes itself as "a self-managed real estate investment trust (REIT)
  that acquires, manages, and develops a diversified portfolio of real estate, primarily
  multi-tenant shopping centers." As of December 31, 2009 its portfolio consisted of 299
  consolidated operating properties (242 wholly owned, 57 in three majority-owned joint
  ventures), plus interests in 11 further unconsolidated joint-venture properties and
  several development properties. [SRC: SEC accession 0001222840-10-000004, Form 10-K FY2009]
- The entity was formed in 2003 with no employees of its own; it had agreements under
  which related parties (a business manager/advisor and property managers) provided all
  services and staff for fees. On November 15, 2007 the entity acquired those related
  parties in exchange for 37,500 newly issued shares of its stock (with 55% escrowed),
  making the former business manager/advisor and property managers its subsidiaries — an
  "internalization" that predates the drawn filing by roughly three years.
  [SRC: SEC accession 0001222840-10-000004, Form 10-K FY2009]

## Structural summary (closing-era only)
- The drawn filing and its immediate contemporaneous 8-Ks establish routine governance,
  compensation, distribution, and (in one instance) a rejected unsolicited partial tender
  offer — none of them a business-combination or roll-up closing. The entity's own
  closing-era annual report describes an ongoing, multi-property, joint-venture-based
  acquisition and financing program (hundreds of properties accumulated over several
  years, plus a newly entered joint venture in 2010) rather than a single discrete
  acquisition transaction dated to this filing. No S-4/DEFM14A merger document was found
  for 2010. [SRC: SEC accession 0001104659-10-052516, Form 8-K Ex-99.1] [SRC: SEC accession 0001222840-10-000004, Form 10-K FY2009]

[SLICE END]
